## P2 - Resubscribe/gap-recovery path is unreachable because `ErrorCallback` keeps the netlink subscription alive

**Location:** [core/events/netlink.go:372-435](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/2e29fac504a97d551c4efcc4ca87683b16f263a4/core/events/netlink.go#L372-L435)

**Problem:** `watch` sets `ErrorCallback` on `netlink.LinkSubscribeOptions` and treats a closed `updates` channel &#40;`case !ok`&#41; as the subscription-end signal that drives resubscription in `run`. In `github.com/vishvananda/netlink` v1.3.1, a registered receive-error handler makes the library&#39;s subscription goroutine call the callback and continue its receive loop instead of returning, so `updates` only closes via `defer close(done)` — which runs when `watch` is already returning on `ctx.Done()`. The `!ok` branch is therefore unreachable in production&#58; the resubscribe loop never fires after a successful subscription, `lastError`/`errMu` are never read, and the gap-recovery design &#40;`processExisting` with `initial=false`, `removeVanishedLinks`&#41; is dead code.

**Trigger:** A netlink receive error on the subscription socket in steady state, for example `ENOBUFS` when the socket buffer overflows under a burst of link `events` in a large lab. The subscription keeps delivering subsequent messages &#40;an improvement over base, which silently died on the first error&#41;, but notifications dropped by the error are never reconciled.

**Impact:** The PR&#39;s headline feature — automatic resubscription and gap reconciliation — never engages, so `events` output can silently diverge from reality after dropped notifications&#58; a deleted link stays in `states` forever with no `delete` event, and missed attribute changes only surface if a later notification happens to differ from the stale state. No test can exercise the resubscribe path because it cannot occur.

**Suggested correction:** Drop `ErrorCallback` &#40;and with it `lastError`/`errMu`&#41; so a `Receive` error makes the library goroutine return and close `updates`; the already-implemented `!ok` → resubscribe → re-list → reconcile flow then works as designed, and interrupted listings self-heal via the re-listing on the next attempt. Confirm against the v1.3.1 module source before merging, and consider a one-line note in [`docs/cmd/events.md`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/2e29fac504a97d551c4efcc4ca87683b16f263a4/docs/cmd/events.md#L1-L1) that after a resubscribe pre-existing interfaces are re-reported as `create` `events`.


## P4 - `removeVanishedLinks` can race with queued listing replies after a resubscribe, emitting a false `create`

**Location:** [core/events/netlink.go:394-396](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/2e29fac504a97d551c4efcc4ca87683b16f263a4/core/events/netlink.go#L394-L396)

**Problem:** After a resubscribe, `NLM_F_MULTI` listing replies for a dump taken at subscribe time may still be queued while `removeVanishedLinks` separately calls `LinkList` to detect links deleted during the subscription-less gap. If a tracked link is deleted between the dump generation and the `LinkList` &#40;its `RTM_DELLINK` lost in the gap&#41;, `removeVanishedLinks` emits `delete` and removes it from `states`, but the stale listing reply then makes `processExisting` emit a false `create` and re-add it to `states`, where it lingers. Conversely, a deletion landing after the `LinkList` but before the dump is processed yields no `delete` event at all. Both variants stem from reconciling with two independently taken snapshots.

**Trigger:** Only reachable once the P2 fix activates the resubscribe path; a link deletion landing in the milliseconds-wide window between the subscription&#39;s dump snapshot and the `removeVanishedLinks` listing.

**Impact:** One spurious `create` event per race occurrence plus a stale `states` entry that persists until the interface index is reused; cosmetic event-stream inaccuracy with no resource growth.

**Suggested correction:** Drive reconciliation from a single source of truth&#58; `run` `removeVanishedLinks` only after the listing replies have been consumed, or derive deletes from the listing itself. Optional improvement given the narrow window.


## Coverage

- Both changed paths were reviewed in full&#58; [`head/core/events/netlink.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/2e29fac504a97d551c4efcc4ca87683b16f263a4/core/events/netlink.go#L1-L1) &#40;all 1216 lines including `run`, `watch`, `processExisting`, `removeVanishedLinks`, `processUpdate`, `pollNetemChanges`, `collectAndEmitStats`, and the netem querier&#41;, the new [`netlink_watch_test.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/2e29fac504a97d551c4efcc4ca87683b16f263a4/core/events/netlink_watch_test.go#L1-L1) &#40;all 375 lines&#41;, base `netlink.go` regions from `diff.txt`, plus [`core/events/stream.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/2e29fac504a97d551c4efcc4ca87683b16f263a4/core/events/stream.go#L1-L1), `types.go`, `netlink_test.go` &#40;no helper-name collisions with the new test file&#41;, [`go.mod`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/2e29fac504a97d551c4efcc4ca87683b16f263a4/go.mod#L1-L1), and [`docs/cmd/events.md`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/2e29fac504a97d551c4efcc4ca87683b16f263a4/docs/cmd/events.md#L1-L1).
- The vishvananda/netlink v1.3.1 source is not vendored in the snapshot; the P2 analysis of `ErrorCallback`/channel-close semantics is based on the library&#39;s subscribe implementation as known for this version, corroborated by the PR&#39;s own comment acknowledging that the callback absorbs listing errors. Verify against the module source before merging.
- Tests were not executed &#40;source-only review&#41;. The new integration tests require root and real network namespaces; their netns lifecycle handling &#40;`LockOSThread`, cleanup ordering, non-Fatal `t.Errorf` inside the `wg.Go` goroutine&#41; was inspected and is correct.
- No test exercises resubscription after a live subscription error; with the P2 finding, such a test cannot pass until the `ErrorCallback` is removed.
- No topology/configuration API changes are involved, so no schema comparison was needed. The PR adds no doc changes; if resubscription becomes active, [`docs/cmd/events.md`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/2e29fac504a97d551c4efcc4ca87683b16f263a4/docs/cmd/events.md#L1-L1) could mention the create-after-resubscribe behavior and the final Warn when giving up after `watchMaxAttempts` failures.
- Tests mutate package-level `watchRetryDelay`/`watchMaxAttempts` with `t.Cleanup` restore; currently safe because no test in the package uses `t.Parallel`&#40;&#41;, but this would race if parallelization is added later.

1: ---
2: description: Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Use when writing, reviewing, or refactoring code to avoid overcomplication, make surgical changes, surface assumptions, and define verifiable success criteria.
3: alwaysApply: true
4: ---
5: 
6: # Karpathy behavioral guidelines
7: 
8: Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Merge with project-specific instructions as needed.
9: 
10: **Tradeoff:** These guidelines bias toward caution over speed. For trivial tasks, use judgment.
11: 
12: ## 1. Think Before Coding
13: 
14: **Don't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.**
15: 
16: Before implementing:
17: 
18: - State your assumptions explicitly. If uncertain, ask.
19: - If multiple interpretations exist, present them - don't pick silently.
20: - If a simpler approach exists, say so. Push back when warranted.
21: - If something is unclear, stop. Name what's confusing. Ask.
22: 
23: ## 2. Simplicity First
24: 
25: **Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.**
26: 
27: - No features beyond what was asked.
28: - No abstractions for single-use code.
29: - No "flexibility" or "configurability" that wasn't requested.
30: - No error handling for impossible scenarios.
31: - If you write 200 lines and it could be 50, rewrite it.
32: 
33: Ask yourself: "Would a senior engineer say this is overcomplicated?" If yes, simplify.
34: 
35: ## 3. Surgical Changes
36: 
37: **Touch only what you must. Clean up only your own mess.**
38: 
39: When editing existing code:
40: 
41: - Don't "improve" adjacent code, comments, or formatting.
42: - Don't refactor things that aren't broken.
43: - Match existing style, even if you'd do it differently.
44: - If you notice unrelated dead code, mention it - don't delete it.
45: 
46: When your changes create orphans:
47: 
48: - Remove imports/variables/functions that YOUR changes made unused.
49: - Don't remove pre-existing dead code unless asked.
50: 
51: The test: Every changed line should trace directly to the user's request.
52: 
53: ## 4. Goal-Driven Execution
54: 
55: **Define success criteria. Loop until verified.**
56: 
57: Transform tasks into verifiable goals:
58: 
59: - "Add validation" → "Write tests for invalid inputs, then make them pass"
60: - "Fix the bug" → "Write a test that reproduces it, then make it pass"
61: - "Refactor X" → "Ensure tests pass before and after"
62: 
63: For multi-step tasks, state a brief plan:
64: 
65: ```
66: 1. [Step] → verify: [check]
67: 2. [Step] → verify: [check]
68: 3. [Step] → verify: [check]
69: ```
70: 
71: Strong success criteria let you loop independently. Weak criteria ("make it work") require constant clarification.
72: 
73: ---
74: 
75: **These guidelines are working if:** fewer unnecessary changes in diffs, fewer rewrites due to overcomplication, and clarifying questions come before implementation rather than after mistakes.

1: ---
2: description: Ponytail, lazy senior dev mode. Always pick the simplest solution that works.
3: globs:
4: alwaysApply: true
5: ---
6: 
7: # Ponytail, lazy senior dev mode
8: 
9: You are a lazy senior developer. Lazy means efficient, not careless. The best code is the code never written.
10: 
11: Before writing any code, stop at the first rung that holds:
12: 
13: 1. Does this need to be built at all? (YAGNI)
14: 2. Does it already exist in this codebase? Reuse the helper, util, or pattern that's already here, don't re-write it.
15: 3. Does the standard library already do this? Use it.
16: 4. Does a native platform feature cover it? Use it.
17: 5. Does an already-installed dependency solve it? Use it.
18: 6. Can this be one line? Make it one line.
19: 7. Only then: write the minimum code that works.
20: 
21: The ladder runs after you understand the problem, not instead of it: read the task and the code it touches, trace the real flow end to end, then climb.
22: 
23: Bug fix = root cause, not symptom: a report names a symptom. Grep every caller of the function you touch and fix the shared function once — one guard there is a smaller diff than one per caller, and patching only the path the ticket names leaves a sibling caller still broken.
24: 
25: Rules:
26: 
27: - No abstractions that weren't explicitly requested.
28: - No new dependency if it can be avoided.
29: - No boilerplate nobody asked for.
30: - Deletion over addition. Boring over clever. Fewest files possible.
31: - Shortest working diff wins, but only once you understand the problem. The smallest change in the wrong place isn't lazy, it's a second bug.
32: - Question complex requests: "Do you actually need X, or does Y cover it?"
33: - Pick the edge-case-correct option when two stdlib approaches are the same size, lazy means less code, not the flimsier algorithm.
34: - Mark deliberate simplifications that cut a real corner with a known ceiling (global lock, O(n²) scan, naive heuristic) with a `ponytail:` comment naming the ceiling and upgrade path.
35: 
36: Not lazy about: understanding the problem (read it fully and trace the real flow before picking a rung, a small diff you don't understand is just laziness dressed up as efficiency), input validation at trust boundaries, error handling that prevents data loss, security, accessibility, the calibration real hardware needs (the platform is never the spec ideal, a clock drifts, a sensor reads off), anything explicitly requested. Lazy code without its check is unfinished: non-trivial logic leaves ONE runnable check behind, the smallest thing that fails if the logic breaks (an assert-based demo/self-check or one small test file; no frameworks, no fixtures). Trivial one-liners need no test.

(End of file - total 36 lines)
</content>

417: +// eventLog collects the interface events of a registry by interface name.
418: +type eventLog struct {
419: +	mu      sync.Mutex
420: +	actions map[string][]string
421: +}
422: +
423: +func collectEvents(ctx context.Context, events <-chan aggregatedEvent) *eventLog {
424: +	l := &eventLog{actions: map[string][]string{}}
425: +
426: +	go func() {
427: +		for {
428: +			select {
429: +			case ev := <-events:
430: +				l.mu.Lock()
431: +				name := ev.Attributes["ifname"]
432: +				l.actions[name] = append(l.actions[name], ev.Action)
433: +				l.mu.Unlock()
434: +			case <-ctx.Done():
435: +				return
436: +			}
437: +		}
438: +	}()
439: +
440: +	return l
441: +}
442: +
443: +func (l *eventLog) get(name string) []string {
444: +	l.mu.Lock()
445: +	defer l.mu.Unlock()
446: +
447: +	return slices.Clone(l.actions[name])
448: +}
449: +
450: +// waitFor waits until every name has an event with one of the actions.
451: +func (l *eventLog) waitFor(t *testing.T, names []string, actions ...string) {
452: +	t.Helper()
453: +
454: +	deadline := time.Now().Add(3 * time.Second)
455: +	for {
456: +		var missing []string
457: +		for _, name := range names {
458: +			if !slices.ContainsFunc(l.get(name), func(a string) bool {
459: +				return slices.Contains(actions, a)
460: +			}) {
461: +				missing = append(missing, name)
462: +			}
463: +		}
464: +
465: +		if len(missing) == 0 {
466: +			return
467: +		}
468: +
469: +		if time.Now().After(deadline) {
470: +			t.Fatalf("no %v event for %v", actions, missing)
471: +		}
472: +
473: +		time.Sleep(10 * time.Millisecond)
474: +	}
475: +}

477: +// newTestNetns creates a named network namespace without leaving the
478: +// current thread in it.
479: +func newTestNetns(t *testing.T) (string, *netlink.Handle) {
480: +	t.Helper()
481: +
482: +	if os.Geteuid() != 0 {
483: +		t.Skip("requires root to create network namespaces")
484: +	}
485: +
486: +	runtime.LockOSThread()
487: +	defer runtime.UnlockOSThread()
488: +
489: +	orig, err := netns.Get()
490: +	if err != nil {
491: +		t.Fatalf("failed to get current netns: %v", err)
492: +	}
493: +	defer orig.Close()
494: +
495: +	name := fmt.Sprintf("clabtst-ev-%d-%d", os.Getpid(), time.Now().UnixNano())
496: +
497: +	ns, err := netns.NewNamed(name)
498: +	if err != nil {
499: +		t.Fatalf("failed to create netns: %v", err)
500: +	}
501: +
502: +	if err := netns.Set(orig); err != nil {
503: +		t.Fatalf("failed to return to the original netns: %v", err)
504: +	}
505: +
506: +	handle, err := netlink.NewHandleAt(ns)
507: +	if err != nil {
508: +		t.Fatalf("failed to create netlink handle: %v", err)
509: +	}
510: +
511: +	t.Cleanup(func() {
512: +		handle.Close()
513: +		ns.Close()
514: +		_ = netns.DeleteNamed(name)
515: +	})
516: +
517: +	return "/run/netns/" + name, handle
518: +}

329: // them until ctx ends or the subscription fails. It reports whether it

420: 		case <-netemTicker.C:
421: 			w.pollNetemChanges(states, registry, netemQuery)
422: 		case <-ctx.Done():
423: 			return true, nil
424: 		case update, ok := <-updates:
425: 			if !ok {
426: 				errMu.Lock()
427: 				err := lastError
428: 				errMu.Unlock()
429: 
430: 				if err == nil {
431: 					err = errors.New("update channel closed")
432: 				}
433: 
434: 				return true, err
435: 			}
436: 
437: 			// Replies to the listing carry NLM_F_MULTI, notifications do not.
438: 			if update.Header.Flags&unix.NLM_F_MULTI != 0 {
439: 				w.processExisting(states, statsSamples, update.Link, netemInfos, registry, initial)
440: 
441: 				continue
442: 			}
443: 
444: 			w.processUpdate(states, statsSamples, update, registry, netemQuery)
445: 		}
446: 	}
447: }

449: // processExisting records a link listed when the subscription started. On the
450: // first subscription a new link is reported as a snapshot when requested; after
451: // a resubscribe it is reported as created.
452: func (w *netlinkWatcher) processExisting(
453: 	states map[int]ifaceSnapshot,
454: 	statsSamples map[int]ifaceStatsSample,
455: 	link netlink.Link,
456: 	netemInfos map[int]netemInfo,
457: 	registry *netlinkRegistry,
458: 	initial bool,
459: ) {
460: 	if link == nil || link.Attrs() == nil {
461: 		return
462: 	}
463: 
464: 	snapshot := withNetem(snapshotFromLink(link), netemInfos)
465: 	previous, exists := states[snapshot.Index]
466: 
467: 	if exists && snapshot.equal(previous) {
468: 		return
469: 	}
470: 
471: 	states[snapshot.Index] = snapshot
472: 	if statsSamples != nil {
473: 		if sample, ok := newStatsSample(snapshot, time.Now()); ok {
474: 			statsSamples[snapshot.Index] = sample
475: 		}
476: 	}
477: 
478: 	switch {
479: 	case exists:
480: 		registry.emitInterfaceEvent(w.container, "update", snapshot)
481: 	case !initial:
482: 		registry.emitInterfaceEvent(w.container, "create", snapshot)
483: 	case w.includeSnapshot:
484: 		registry.emitInterfaceEvent(w.container, "snapshot", snapshot)
485: 	}
486: }
487: 
488: // removeVanishedLinks reports the links that were deleted while no
489: // subscription was active.
490: func (w *netlinkWatcher) removeVanishedLinks(
491: 	netHandle *netlink.Handle,
492: 	states map[int]ifaceSnapshot,
493: 	statsSamples map[int]ifaceStatsSample,
494: 	registry *netlinkRegistry,
495: ) {
496: 	current, err := snapshotInterfaces(netHandle)
497: 	if err != nil {
498: 		log.Debugf(
499: 			"failed to list interfaces of container %s: %v",
500: 			firstContainerName(w.container),
501: 			err,
502: 		)
503: 
504: 		return
505: 	}
506: 
507: 	for idx, snapshot := range states {
508: 		if _, ok := current[idx]; ok {
509: 			continue
510: 		}
511: 
512: 		delete(states, idx)
513: 		delete(statsSamples, idx)
514: 		registry.emitInterfaceEvent(w.container, "delete", snapshot)
515: 	}
516: }
517: 
518: func (w *netlinkWatcher) processUpdate(
519: 	states map[int]ifaceSnapshot,
520: 	statsSamples map[int]ifaceStatsSample,
521: 	update netlink.LinkUpdate,
522: 	registry *netlinkRegistry,
523: 	netemQuery *netemQuerier,
524: ) {
525: 	if update.Link == nil {
526: 		return
527: 	}
528: 
529: 	attrs := update.Link.Attrs()
530: 	if attrs == nil {
531: 		return
532: 	}
533: 
534: 	snapshot := snapshotFromLink(update.Link)
535: 	previous, exists := states[snapshot.Index]
536: 
537: 	switch update.Header.Type {
538: 	case unix.RTM_DELLINK:
539: 		// A link that is not tracked was never reported, or its deletion was
540: 		// already reported when the links were listed again after a resubscribe.
541: 		if !exists {
542: 			return
543: 		}
544: 
545: 		delete(states, snapshot.Index)
546: 		delete(statsSamples, snapshot.Index)
547: 		registry.emitInterfaceEvent(w.container, "delete", previous)
548: 	case unix.RTM_NEWLINK:
549: 		// Query netem info for this interface
550: 		snapshot = withNetem(snapshot, netemQuery.Query())
551: 
552: 		if exists && snapshot.equal(previous) {
553: 			return
554: 		}
555: 
556: 		action := "create"
557: 		if exists {
558: 			action = "update"
559: 		}
560: 
561: 		states[snapshot.Index] = snapshot
562: 		if w.includeStats && statsSamples != nil {
563: 			if sample, ok := newStatsSample(snapshot, time.Now()); ok {
564: 				statsSamples[snapshot.Index] = sample
565: 			}
566: 		}
567: 		registry.emitInterfaceEvent(w.container, action, snapshot)
568: 	}
569: }
570: 
571: // pollNetemChanges checks for netem changes and emits update events.
572: func (w *netlinkWatcher) pollNetemChanges(
573: 	states map[int]ifaceSnapshot,
574: 	registry *netlinkRegistry,
575: 	netemQuery *netemQuerier,
576: ) {
577: 	netemInfos := netemQuery.Query()
578: 
579: 	for idx, snapshot := range states {
580: 		previous := snapshot
581: 		info, hasNetem := netemInfos[idx]
582: 
583: 		if hasNetem {
584: 			snapshot.HasNetem = true
585: 			snapshot.Delay = info.Delay
586: 			snapshot.Jitter = info.Jitter
587: 			snapshot.PacketLoss = info.PacketLoss
588: 			snapshot.Rate = info.Rate
589: 			snapshot.Corruption = info.Corruption
590: 		} else if snapshot.HasNetem {
591: 			// Netem was removed
592: 			snapshot.HasNetem = false
593: 			snapshot.Delay = ""
594: 			snapshot.Jitter = ""
595: 			snapshot.PacketLoss = 0
596: 			snapshot.Rate = 0
597: 			snapshot.Corruption = 0
598: 		}
599: 
600: 		if !snapshot.equal(previous) {
601: 			states[idx] = snapshot
602: 			registry.emitInterfaceEvent(w.container, "update", snapshot)
603: 		}
604: 	}
605: }

607: func firstContainerName(container *clabruntime.GenericContainer) string {
608: 	if container == nil || len(container.Names) == 0 {
609: 		return ""
610: 	}
611: 
612: 	return container.Names[0]
613: }

615: func containerLabel(container *clabruntime.GenericContainer) string {
616: 	if container == nil || container.Labels == nil {
617: 		return ""
618: 	}
619: 
620: 	return container.Labels[clabconstants.Containerlab]
621: }

623: func interfaceAttributes(
624: 	container *clabruntime.GenericContainer,
625: 	snapshot ifaceSnapshot,
626: ) map[string]string {
627: 	attributes := map[string]string{
628: 		"ifname": snapshot.Name,
629: 		"index":  strconv.Itoa(snapshot.Index),
630: 		"mtu":    strconv.Itoa(snapshot.MTU),
631: 		"state":  snapshot.OperState,
632: 		"type":   snapshot.Type,
633: 		"origin": "netlink",
634: 	}
635: 
636: 	if snapshot.Alias != "" {
637: 		attributes["alias"] = snapshot.Alias
638: 	}
639: 
640: 	if snapshot.MAC != "" {
641: 		attributes["mac"] = snapshot.MAC
642: 	}
643: 
644: 	if lab := containerLabel(container); lab != "" {
645: 		attributes["lab"] = lab
646: 	}
647: 
648: 	if name := firstContainerName(container); name != "" {
649: 		attributes["name"] = name
650: 	}
651: 
652: 	overlayToolsInterface(container, attributes)
653: 
654: 	// Add netem attributes if present
655: 	if snapshot.HasNetem {
656: 		if snapshot.Delay != "" {
657: 			attributes["netem_delay"] = snapshot.Delay
658: 		}
659: 		if snapshot.Jitter != "" {
660: 			attributes["netem_jitter"] = snapshot.Jitter
661: 		}
662: 		if snapshot.PacketLoss != 0 {
663: 			attributes["netem_loss"] = strconv.FormatFloat(snapshot.PacketLoss, 'f', 2, 64) + "%"
664: 		}
665: 		if snapshot.Rate != 0 {
666: 			attributes["netem_rate"] = strconv.Itoa(snapshot.Rate) + "kbit"
667: 		}
668: 		if snapshot.Corruption != 0 {
669: 			attributes["netem_corruption"] = strconv.FormatFloat(
670: 				snapshot.Corruption,
671: 				'f',
672: 				2,
673: 				64,
674: 			) + "%"
675: 		}
676: 	}
677: 
678: 	return attributes
679: }

681: // overlayToolsInterface rewrites attributes to the host-side stitch interface
682: // when one exists, matching `inspect interfaces`.
683: func overlayToolsInterface(
684: 	container *clabruntime.GenericContainer,
685: 	attributes map[string]string,
686: ) {
687: 	if container == nil {
688: 		return
689: 	}
690: 
691: 	lab, node := clabcore.TopoIdentity(container.Labels)
692: 	if lab == "" || node == "" {
693: 		return
694: 	}
695: 
696: 	topoName := attributes["alias"]
697: 	if topoName == "" {
698: 		topoName = attributes["ifname"]
699: 	}

746: func waitForNamespacePath(
747: 	ctx context.Context,
748: 	runtime clabruntime.ContainerRuntime,
749: 	containerID string,
750: ) (string, error) {
751: 	const (
752: 		attempts   = 5
753: 		retryDelay = 200 * time.Millisecond
754: 	)
755: 
756: 	var lastErr error
757: 
758: 	for i := 0; i < attempts; i++ {
759: 		nsPath, err := runtime.GetNSPath(ctx, containerID)
760: 		if err == nil && nsPath != "" {
761: 			return nsPath, nil
762: 		}
763: 
764: 		if err != nil {
765: 			lastErr = err
766: 		}
767: 
768: 		select {
769: 		case <-time.After(retryDelay):
770: 		case <-ctx.Done():
771: 			return "", ctx.Err()
772: 		}
773: 	}
774: 
775: 	if lastErr != nil {
776: 		return "", lastErr
777: 	}
778: 
779: 	return "", fmt.Errorf("namespace path not ready for container %s", containerID)
780: }

818: func snapshotInterfaces(netHandle *netlink.Handle) (map[int]ifaceSnapshot, error) {
819: 	if netHandle == nil {
820: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("netlink handle is nil")
821: 	}
822: 
823: 	links, err := netHandle.LinkList()
824: 	if err != nil {
825: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("unable to list links: %w", err)
826: 	}
827: 
828: 	states := make(map[int]ifaceSnapshot, len(links))
829: 	for _, link := range links {
830: 		snapshot := snapshotFromLink(link)
831: 		states[snapshot.Index] = snapshot
832: 	}
833: 
834: 	return states, nil
835: }

416: 		action := "create"

432: func (w *netlinkWatcher) pollNetemChanges(
433: 	states map[int]ifaceSnapshot,

436: ) {
437: 	netemInfos := netemQuery.Query()
438: 
439: 	for idx, snapshot := range states {
440: 		previous := snapshot
441: 		info, hasNetem := netemInfos[idx]
442: 
443: 		if hasNetem {
444: 			snapshot.HasNetem = true
445: 			snapshot.Delay = info.Delay
446: 			snapshot.Jitter = info.Jitter
447: 			snapshot.PacketLoss = info.PacketLoss
448: 			snapshot.Rate = info.Rate
449: 			snapshot.Corruption = info.Corruption
450: 		} else if snapshot.HasNetem {
451: 			// Netem was removed
452: 			snapshot.HasNetem = false
453: 			snapshot.Delay = ""
454: 			snapshot.Jitter = ""
455: 			snapshot.PacketLoss = 0
456: 			snapshot.Rate = 0
457: 			snapshot.Corruption = 0
458: 		}
459: 
460: 		if !snapshot.equal(previous) {
461: 			states[idx] = snapshot
462: 			registry.emitInterfaceEvent(w.container, "update", snapshot)
463: 		}
464: 	}
465: }

606: func waitForNamespacePath(
607: 	ctx context.Context,
608: 	runtime clabruntime.ContainerRuntime,
609: 	containerID string,
610: ) (string, error) {
611: 	const (
612: 		attempts   = 5
613: 		retryDelay = 200 * time.Millisecond
614: 	)
615: 
616: 	var lastErr error
617: 
618: 	for i := 0; i < attempts; i++ {
619: 		nsPath, err := runtime.GetNSPath(ctx, containerID)
620: 		if err == nil && nsPath != "" {
621: 			return nsPath, nil
622: 		}
623: 
624: 		if err != nil {
625: 			lastErr = err
626: 		}
627: 
628: 		select {
629: 		case <-time.After(retryDelay):
630: 		case <-ctx.Done():
631: 			return "", ctx.Err()
632: 		}
633: 	}
634: 
635: 	if lastErr != nil {
636: 		return "", lastErr
637: 	}
638: 
639: 	return "", fmt.Errorf("namespace path not ready for container %s", containerID)
640: }

// LinkSubscribeWithOptions take a chan and subscribe
// to netlink link events. If done channel is closed, the subscription
// is cancelled. If ListExisting is true, a dump is performed and all existing
// links are sent to the channel before the subscription is activated.
func LinkSubscribeWithOptions(ch chan<- LinkUpdate, done <-chan struct{}, options LinkSubscribeOptions) error {
	s, _ := nl.GetNetlinkSocketAt(options.Namespace, options.NetNSFd, unix.NETLINK_ROUTE)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	if options.ListExisting {
		err = s.SendMultipartHeader(nl.NewRtMsg(unix.RTM_GETLINK, unix.NLM_F_DUMP))
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}

	// netlink.AllNCDevGroup (0x400) needs to be set to see network
	// devices created in other netcases (containers)...
	if err := nl.Subscribe(s, options.ErrorCallback, unix.RTNLGRP_LINK, unix.RTNLGRP_IPV4_IFADDR, unix.RTNLGRP_IPV6_IFADDR); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	...
}
```

Actually, from real netlink source (subscribe.go), the shared `subscribe`-ish code:

```go
func linkSubscribe(s *nl.NetlinkSocket, ch chan<- LinkUpdate, done <-chan struct{}, options LinkSubscribeOptions) {
	defer close(ch)
	for {
		msgs, from, err := s.Receive()
		if err != nil {
			if done != nil {
				select {
				case <-done:
					return
				default:
				}
			}
			if s.GetReceiveErrorFunc() != nil {
				// Pending error callback is set, so call it and do not return
				s.HandleReceiveError(err)
				continue
			}
			// error is not misbehavior, perhaps the socket was closed
			return
		}
		if len(msgs) == 0 {
			continue
		}

		for _, m := range msgs {
			if m.Header.Type == unix.NLMSG_DONE || m.Header.Type == unix.NLMSG_ERROR {
				// ignore
				continue
			}
			update, err := parseLink(m)
			if err != nil {
				continue
			}
			if done != nil {
				select {
				case ch <- update:
				case <-done:
					return
				}
			} else {
				ch <- update
			}
		}
	}
}
```

This is approximately right — importantly, sends select on done, so when `watch` closes `done`, the goroutine returns and closes `ch`. Good, no goroutine leak concern from the send side.

Key detail: NLMSG_DONE and NLMSG_ERROR messages are skipped (not delivered to ch). And parseLink errors skip non-link messages. So the code's MULTI check applies only to RTM_NEWLINK messages delivered. Dump replies (RTM_NEWLINK with NLM_F_MULTI) → processExisting. Async notifications (RTM_NEWLINK/RTM_DELLINK without MULTI) → processUpdate. That matches kernel behavior.

1: # events command
2: 
3: ## Description
4: 
5: The `events` command streams lifecycle updates for every Containerlab resource and augments them with interface change notifications collected from the container network namespaces. The output combines the selected runtime's event feed (for example Docker) with the netlink information that powers `containerlab inspect interfaces`, so you can observe container activity and interface state changes in real time without selecting a specific lab.
6: 
7: ## Usage
8: 
9: `containerlab [global-flags] events [local-flags]`
10: 
11: **aliases:** `ev`
12: 
13: The command respects the global flags such as `--runtime`, `--debug`, or `--log-level`. It adds local options:
14: 
15: - `--format` controls the output representation (`plain`, `json`).
16: - `--initial-state` emits a snapshot of currently running containers and their interface states before following live updates.
17: - `--interface-stats` enables periodic interface counter sampling; leave unset to report only lifecycle and state changes.
18: - `--interface-stats-interval` customizes how frequently statistics are collected (for example `500ms`, `2s`, `1m`).
19: 
20: When invoked with no arguments it discovers all running labs and immediately begins streaming events; new labs that start after the command begins are picked up automatically.
21: 
22: ## Event format
23: 
24: In the default `plain` format every line mirrors the `docker events` format:
25: 
26: ```
27: <timestamp> <type> <action> <actor> (<key>=<value>, ...)
28: ```
29: 
30: - **Runtime events** show the short container ID as the actor and include the original attributes supplied by the container runtime (for example `image`, `name`, `containerlab`, `scope`, …). Container events are also enriched with `mgmt_ipv4`, `mgmt_ipv6`, and `ports` (published/exposed ports) when those values are available. When `--initial-state` is enabled the stream starts with `container <state>` snapshots (for example `container running`) that carry an `origin=snapshot` attribute.
31: - **Interface events** use type `interface` and `origin=netlink` in the attribute list. They also report interface-specific data such as `ifname`, `state`, `mtu`, `mac`, `type`, `alias`, and the lab label. The actor is still the container short ID, and the container name is supplied in the attributes (`name=...`).
32: - Interface notifications are emitted when a link appears, disappears, or when its relevant properties (operational state, MTU, alias, MAC address, type) change. Initial snapshots use the `snapshot` action when `--initial-state` is requested. When interface statistics are enabled the stream also includes `interface stats` updates with byte/packet counters and rate estimates.
33: 
34: When `--format json` is used, each event becomes a single JSON object on its own line. The fields match the plain output (`timestamp`, `type`, `action`, `actor_id`, `actor_name`, `actor_full_id`) and include an `attributes` map with the same key/value pairs that the plain formatter prints.
35: 
36: ## Examples
37: 
38: ### Watch an existing lab and new deployments
39: 
40: ```
41: $ containerlab events
42: 2024-07-01T11:02:56.123456000Z container start 5d0b5a9ad3f1 (containerlab=frr-lab, image=ghcr.io/srl-labs/frr, name=clab-frr-lab-frr01, ports=0.0.0.0:2222/tcp->22;0.0.0.0:830/tcp->830)
43: 2024-07-01T11:02:57.004321000Z interface create 5d0b5a9ad3f1 (ifname=eth0, index=22, lab=frr-lab, mac=02:42:ac:14:00:02, mtu=1500, name=clab-frr-lab-frr01, origin=netlink, state=up, type=veth)
44: 2024-07-01T11:02:57.104512000Z interface update 5d0b5a9ad3f1 (ifname=eth0, index=22, lab=frr-lab, mac=02:42:ac:14:00:02, mtu=9000, name=clab-frr-lab-frr01, origin=netlink, state=up, type=veth)
45: 2024-07-01T11:05:12.918273000Z container die 5d0b5a9ad3f1 (containerlab=frr-lab, exitCode=0, image=ghcr.io/srl-labs/frr, name=clab-frr-lab-frr01)
46: 2024-07-01T11:05:13.018456000Z interface delete 5d0b5a9ad3f1 (ifname=eth0, index=22, lab=frr-lab, name=clab-frr-lab-frr01, origin=netlink, state=up, type=veth)
47: ```
48: 
49: The stream contains all currently running labs and stays active to capture subsequent deployments, restarts, or interface adjustments.
50: 
51: ### Include existing resources in the stream
52: 
53: ```
54: $ containerlab events --initial-state
55: 2024-07-01T11:02:55.912345000Z container running 5d0b5a9ad3f1 (containerlab=frr-lab, image=ghcr.io/srl-labs/frr, name=clab-frr-lab-frr01, origin=snapshot, ports=0.0.0.0:2222/tcp->22;0.0.0.0:830/tcp->830, state=running)
56: 2024-07-01T11:02:55.912678000Z interface snapshot 5d0b5a9ad3f1 (ifname=eth0, index=22, lab=frr-lab, mac=02:42:ac:14:00:02, mtu=1500, name=clab-frr-lab-frr01, origin=netlink, state=up, type=veth)
57: …
58: ```
59: 
60: This mode begins with a point-in-time view of every running container and interface before switching to live updates.
61: 
62: ### Include interface statistics
63: 
64: ```
65: containerlab events --interface-stats
66: ```
67: 
68: Statistics are disabled by default. Enabling them augments the feed with periodic counter samples in addition to lifecycle and state changes. Use `--interface-stats-interval` to balance fidelity with overhead: values between `1s` and `5s` work well for most labs, while larger deployments may prefer longer intervals (for example `10s`) to avoid excessive sampling load.
69: 
70: ### Use with alternative runtimes
71: 
72: Containerlab streams events from the runtime selected via the global `--runtime` flag.
73: 
74: Currently supported runtimes:
75: 
76: - `docker`
77: - `c9s`
78: 
79: With `--runtime c9s`, events are backed by kubernetes watches for Clabernetes
80: `Topology` resources and labeled Pods. Interface statistics are sampled inside
81: the device containers, not through local host netlink.
82: 
83: Runtimes that do not implement the `events` API, or are not yet supported by Containerlab, will exit with an explanatory error.
84: 
85: ## See also
86: 
87: - [`inspect interfaces`](inspect/interfaces.md) – produces a point-in-time view of the same interface details that `events` reports continuously.
88: - [Clabernetes containerlab runtime](../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md) - explains how c9s events differ from Docker events.
89: - `docker events` – the raw runtime feed that Containerlab builds upon.

(End of file - total 89 lines)
</content>

func LinkSubscribeWithOptions(ch chan<- LinkUpdate, done <-chan struct{}, options LinkSubscribeOptions) error {
	s, _ := nl.GetNetlinkSocketAt(options.Namespace, options.NetNSFd, unix.NETLINK_ROUTE)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

					}
				} else {

				}

}

22: // eventLog collects the interface events of a registry by interface name.
23: type eventLog struct {
24: 	mu      sync.Mutex
25: 	actions map[string][]string
26: }
27: 
28: func collectEvents(ctx context.Context, events <-chan aggregatedEvent) *eventLog {
29: 	l := &eventLog{actions: map[string][]string{}}
30: 
31: 	go func() {
32: 		for {
33: 			select {
34: 			case ev := <-events:
35: 				l.mu.Lock()
36: 				name := ev.Attributes["ifname"]
37: 				l.actions[name] = append(l.actions[name], ev.Action)
38: 				l.mu.Unlock()
39: 			case <-ctx.Done():
40: 				return
41: 			}
42: 		}
43: 	}()
44: 
45: 	return l
46: }
47: 
48: func (l *eventLog) get(name string) []string {
49: 	l.mu.Lock()
50: 	defer l.mu.Unlock()
51: 
52: 	return slices.Clone(l.actions[name])
53: }
54: 
55: // waitFor waits until every name has an event with one of the actions.
56: func (l *eventLog) waitFor(t *testing.T, names []string, actions ...string) {
57: 	t.Helper()
58: 
59: 	deadline := time.Now().Add(3 * time.Second)
60: 	for {
61: 		var missing []string
62: 		for _, name := range names {
63: 			if !slices.ContainsFunc(l.get(name), func(a string) bool {
64: 				return slices.Contains(actions, a)
65: 			}) {
66: 				missing = append(missing, name)
67: 			}
68: 		}
69: 
70: 		if len(missing) == 0 {
71: 			return
72: 		}
73: 
74: 		if time.Now().After(deadline) {
75: 			t.Fatalf("no %v event for %v", actions, missing)
76: 		}
77: 
78: 		time.Sleep(10 * time.Millisecond)
79: 	}
80: }
81: 
82: // newTestNetns creates a named network namespace without leaving the
83: // current thread in it.
84: func newTestNetns(t *testing.T) (string, *netlink.Handle) {
85: 	t.Helper()
86: 
87: 	if os.Geteuid() != 0 {
88: 		t.Skip("requires root to create network namespaces")
89: 	}
90: 
91: 	runtime.LockOSThread()
92: 	defer runtime.UnlockOSThread()
93: 
94: 	orig, err := netns.Get()
95: 	if err != nil {
96: 		t.Fatalf("failed to get current netns: %v", err)
97: 	}
98: 	defer orig.Close()
99: 
100: 	name := fmt.Sprintf("clabtst-ev-%d-%d", os.Getpid(), time.Now().UnixNano())
101: 
102: 	ns, err := netns.NewNamed(name)
103: 	if err != nil {
104: 		t.Fatalf("failed to create netns: %v", err)
105: 	}
106: 
107: 	if err := netns.Set(orig); err != nil {
108: 		t.Fatalf("failed to return to the original netns: %v", err)
109: 	}
110: 
111: 	handle, err := netlink.NewHandleAt(ns)
112: 	if err != nil {
113: 		t.Fatalf("failed to create netlink handle: %v", err)
114: 	}
115: 
116: 	t.Cleanup(func() {
117: 		handle.Close()
118: 		ns.Close()
119: 		_ = netns.DeleteNamed(name)
120: 	})
121: 
122: 	return "/run/netns/" + name, handle
123: }

155: func startRegistry(
156: 	t *testing.T,
157: 	container *clabruntime.GenericContainer,
158: ) (*netlinkRegistry, *eventLog) {
159: 	t.Helper()
160:

175: // TestNetlinkWatcherReportsExistingAndNewLinks checks that links present at
176: // subscription are reported as snapshots and later ones as created or deleted.
177: func TestNetlinkWatcherReportsExistingAndNewLinks(t *testing.T) {
178: 	nsPath, handle := newTestNetns(t)
179: 	addDummy(t, handle, "early0")
180: 
181: 	container := newTestContainer(t, func() (string, error) { return nsPath, nil })
182: 	_, events := startRegistry(t, container)
183: 
184: 	events.waitFor(t, []string{"lo", "early0"}, "snapshot")
185: 
186: 	addDummy(t, handle, "late0")
187: 	events.waitFor(t, []string{"late0"}, "create")
188: 
189: 	link, err := handle.LinkByName("late0")
190: 	if err != nil {
191: 		t.Fatalf("failed to find late0: %v", err)
192: 	}
193: 
194: 	if err := handle.LinkDel(link); err != nil {
195: 		t.Fatalf("failed to delete late0: %v", err)
196: 	}
197: 
198: 	events.waitFor(t, []string{"late0"}, "delete")
199: 
200: 	if got := events.get("early0"); slices.Contains(got, "create") {
201: 		t.Fatalf("early0 was reported as created: %v", got)
202: 	}
203: }

205: // TestNetlinkWatcherReportsLinksAddedWhileStarting adds links while the
206: // watcher starts. Each link must be reported, whether the watcher lists it or
207: // is notified about it.
208: func TestNetlinkWatcherReportsLinksAddedWhileStarting(t *testing.T) {
209: 	for round := range 20 {

211: 			nsPath, handle := newTestNetns(t)
212: 			container := newTestContainer(t, func() (string, error) { return nsPath, nil })

214: 			names := make([]string, 0, 100)
215: 			for i := range cap(names) {
216: 				names = append(names, fmt.Sprintf("dummy%d", i))
217: 			}
218: 
219: 			var wg sync.WaitGroup
220: 			wg.Go(func() {
221: 				for _, name := range names {
222: 					addDummy(t, handle, name)
223: 				}
224: 			})

226: 			_, events := startRegistry(t, container)

228: 
229: 			events.waitFor(t, names, "snapshot", "create")
230: 		})
231: 	}
232: }

234: // TestNetlinkWatcherRetriesNamespaceLookup checks that the watcher keeps
235: // trying when the namespace is not found within the first attempt.
236: func TestNetlinkWatcherRetriesNamespaceLookup(t *testing.T) {
237: 	nsPath, _ := newTestNetns(t)
238: 
239: 	origDelay := watchRetryDelay
240: 	watchRetryDelay = 10 * time.Millisecond
241: 	t.Cleanup(func() { watchRetryDelay = origDelay })
242: 
243: 	var (
244: 		mu    sync.Mutex
245: 		calls int
246: 	)
247: 
248: 	// waitForNamespacePath asks five times per attempt, so the first attempt fails.
249: 	container := newTestContainer(t, func() (string, error) {
250: 		mu.Lock()
251: 		defer mu.Unlock()
252: 
253: 		calls++
254: 		if calls <= 6 {
255: 			return "", errors.New("not ready")
256: 		}
257: 
258: 		return nsPath, nil
259: 	})
260: 
261: 	_, events := startRegistry(t, container)
262: 	events.waitFor(t, []string{"lo"}, "snapshot")
263: }

265: // TestNetlinkWatcherStopsAfterRetries checks that the watcher gives up when
266: // the namespace is never found.
267: func TestNetlinkWatcherStopsAfterRetries(t *testing.T) {
268: 	origAttempts, origDelay := watchMaxAttempts, watchRetryDelay
269: 	watchMaxAttempts, watchRetryDelay = 2, 10*time.Millisecond
270: 	t.Cleanup(func() { watchMaxAttempts, watchRetryDelay = origAttempts, origDelay })
271: 
272: 	container := newTestContainer(t, func() (string, error) { return "", errors.New("gone") })
273: 	registry, _ := startRegistry(t, container)
274: 
275: 	registry.mu.Lock()
276: 	watcher := registry.watchers[container.ID]
277: 	registry.mu.Unlock()
278: 
279: 	select {
280: 	case <-watcher.done:
281: 	case <-time.After(5 * time.Second):
282: 		t.Fatal("watcher did not stop")
283: 	}
284: }

286: // TestProcessExistingAfterResubscribe checks how a listed link is reported on
287: // the first subscription and after a resubscribe.
288: func TestProcessExistingAfterResubscribe(t *testing.T) {
289: 	link := func(mtu int) netlink.Link {
290: 		return &netlink.Dummy{LinkAttrs: netlink.LinkAttrs{Index: 7, Name: "eth1", MTU: mtu}}
291: 	}
292: 
293: 	tests := map[string]struct {
294: 		includeSnapshot bool
295: 		initial         bool
296: 		known           netlink.Link
297: 		want            []string
298: 	}{
299: 		"first subscription": {
300: 			includeSnapshot: true,
301: 			initial:         true,
302: 			want:            []string{"snapshot"},
303: 		},
304: 		"first subscription without snapshot": {initial: true},
305: 		"new after resubscribe":               {want: []string{"create"}},
306: 		"changed after resubscribe":           {known: link(1400), want: []string{"update"}},
307: 		"unchanged after resubscribe":         {known: link(1500)},
308: 	}
309: 
310: 	for name, tt := range tests {
311: 		t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
312: 			events := make(chan aggregatedEvent, 8)
313: 			registry := newNetlinkRegistry(t.Context(), events, tt.includeSnapshot, false, 0)
314: 			watcher := &netlinkWatcher{
315: 				container:       &clabruntime.GenericContainer{Names: []string{"n1"}},
316: 				includeSnapshot: tt.includeSnapshot,
317: 			}
318: 
319: 			states := map[int]ifaceSnapshot{}
320: 			if tt.known != nil {
321: 				states[7] = snapshotFromLink(tt.known)
322: 			}
323: 
324: 			watcher.processExisting(states, nil, link(1500), nil, registry, tt.initial)
325: 			close(events)
326: 
327: 			var got []string
328: 			for ev := range events {
329: 				got = append(got, ev.Action)
330: 			}
331: 
332: 			if !slices.Equal(got, tt.want) {
333: 				t.Fatalf("actions = %v, want %v", got, tt.want)
334: 			}
335: 
336: 			if states[7].MTU != 1500 {
337: 				t.Fatalf("state MTU = %d, want 1500", states[7].MTU)
338: 			}
339: 		})
340: 	}
341: }

343: // TestProcessUpdateDeleteOnlyTrackedLinks checks that a deletion is reported
344: // once, also when its notification arrives after a resubscribe has already
345: // reported it.
346: func TestProcessUpdateDeleteOnlyTrackedLinks(t *testing.T) {
347: 	link := &netlink.Dummy{LinkAttrs: netlink.LinkAttrs{Index: 7, Name: "eth1", MTU: 1500}}
348: 	update := netlink.LinkUpdate{Link: link}
349: 	update.Header.Type = unix.RTM_DELLINK
350: 
351: 	events := make(chan aggregatedEvent, 8)
352: 	registry := newNetlinkRegistry(t.Context(), events, false, false, 0)
353: 	watcher := &netlinkWatcher{
354: 		container: &clabruntime.GenericContainer{Names: []string{"n1"}},
355: 	}
356: 
357: 	states := map[int]ifaceSnapshot{7: snapshotFromLink(link)}
358: 
359: 	watcher.processUpdate(states, nil, update, registry, nil)
360: 	watcher.processUpdate(states, nil, update, registry, nil)
361: 	close(events)
362: 
363: 	var got []string
364: 	for ev := range events {
365: 		got = append(got, ev.Action)
366: 	}
367: 
368: 	if want := []string{"delete"}; !slices.Equal(got, want) {
369: 		t.Fatalf("actions = %v, want %v", got, want)
370: 	}
371: 
372: 	if _, ok := states[7]; ok {
373: 		t.Fatal("deleted link is still tracked")
374: 	}
375: }

449: // processExisting records a link listed when the subscription started. On the
450: // first subscription a new link is reported as a snapshot when requested; after
451: // a resubscribe it is reported as created.
452: func (w *netlinkWatcher) processExisting(
453: 	states map[int]ifaceSnapshot,
454: 	statsSamples map[int]ifaceStatsSample,
455: 	link netlink.Link,
456: 	netemInfos map[int]netemInfo,
457: 	registry *netlinkRegistry,
458: 	initial bool,

462: 	}
463:

465: 	previous, exists := states[snapshot.Index]
466: 
467: 	if exists && snapshot.equal(previous) {
468: 		return
469: 	}
470: 
471: 	states[snapshot.Index] = snapshot
472: 	if statsSamples != nil {
473: 		if sample, ok := newStatsSample(snapshot, time.Now()); ok {
474: 			statsSamples[snapshot.Index] = sample
475: 		}
476: 	}
477:

479: 	case exists:
480: 		registry.emitInterfaceEvent(w.container, "update", snapshot)
481: 	case !initial:
482: 		registry.emitInterfaceEvent(w.container, "create", snapshot)
483: 	case w.includeSnapshot:
484: 		registry.emitInterfaceEvent(w.container, "snapshot", snapshot)
485: 	}
486: }

499: 			"failed to list interfaces of container %s: %v",
500: 			firstContainerName(w.container),
501: 			err,
502: 		)
503: 
504: 		return
505: 	}
506:

511: 
512: 		delete(states, idx)
513: 		delete(statsSamples, idx)
514: 		registry.emitInterfaceEvent(w.container, "delete", snapshot)
515: 	}

417: +// eventLog collects the interface events of a registry by interface name.
418: +type eventLog struct {
419: +	mu      sync.Mutex
420: +	actions map[string][]string
421: +}
422: +
423: +func collectEvents(ctx context.Context, events <-chan aggregatedEvent) *eventLog {
424: +	l := &eventLog{actions: map[string][]string{}}
425: +
426: +	go func() {
427: +		for {
428: +			select {
429: +			case ev := <-events:
430: +				l.mu.Lock()
431: +				name := ev.Attributes["ifname"]
432: +				l.actions[name] = append(l.actions[name], ev.Action)
433: +				l.mu.Unlock()
434: +			case <-ctx.Done():
435: +				return
436: +			}
437: +		}
438: +	}()
439: +
440: +	return l
441: +}
442: +
443: +func (l *eventLog) get(name string) []string {
444: +	l.mu.Lock()
445: +	defer l.mu.Unlock()
446: +
447: +	return slices.Clone(l.actions[name])
448: +}
449: +
450: +// waitFor waits until every name has an event with one of the actions.
451: +func (l *eventLog) waitFor(t *testing.T, names []string, actions ...string) {
452: +	t.Helper()
453: +
454: +	deadline := time.Now().Add(3 * time.Second)
455: +	for {
456: +		var missing []string
457: +		for _, name := range names {
458: +			if !slices.ContainsFunc(l.get(name), func(a string) bool {
459: +				return slices.Contains(actions, a)
460: +			}) {
461: +				missing = append(missing, name)
462: +			}
463: +		}
464: +
465: +		if len(missing) == 0 {
466: +			return
467: +		}
468: +
469: +		if time.Now().After(deadline) {
470: +			t.Fatalf("no %v event for %v", actions, missing)
471: +		}
472: +
473: +		time.Sleep(10 * time.Millisecond)
474: +	}
475: +}

631: +func TestNetlinkWatcherRetriesNamespaceLookup(t *testing.T) {
632: +	nsPath, _ := newTestNetns(t)

636: +	t.Cleanup(func() { watchRetryDelay = origDelay })

639: +		mu    sync.Mutex
640: +		calls int

644: +	container := newTestContainer(t, func() (string, error) {
645: +		mu.Lock()

Now I have the full picture. Let me finalize the analysis.

Key finding 1 (P2): The resubscribe path in `run` is effectively unreachable because `ErrorCallback` is set on `LinkSubscribeOptions`. In `github.com/vishvananda/netlink` (all recent versions, including v1.3.1 in `head/go.mod`), the subscription goroutine's `Receive()` error handling is: if a receive-error handler (the `ErrorCallback`) is registered, the library calls it and `continue`s the receive loop — it does not return/close the channel. So `updates` is only closed when `done` closes (i.e., when `watch` itself returns after `ctx.Done()`), which is exactly when the caller is already returning. Therefore:
- `case update, ok := <-updates: if !ok {...return true, err}` is unreachable in practice.
- The retry-with-Warn "resubscribing" path never executes after a successful subscription.
- `lastError` is never read (dead state).
- The gap-reconciliation machinery (`removeVanishedLinks` on resubscribe, `processExisting` with `initial=false`) is dead in production; only the first subscription's listing uses it.
- Net effect: the PR's headline resilience feature (recover from lost subscription, reconcile missed changes) doesn't engage; on socket errors (e.g., ENOBUFS buffer overflow), notifications are dropped silently (Debug-logged only) and missed changes are never reconciled. That is an improvement over base (which silently died) but not the designed behavior.

Correction: simplest fix per ponytail rules — drop the `ErrorCallback` so receive errors close the `updates` channel, which drives the resubscribe loop the PR already implements; reconciliation then also covers changes missed during the broken subscription. Alternatively, if the intent is to keep the callback, have it signal termination.

<content>
1: # events command
2: 
3: ## Description
4: 
5: The `events` command streams lifecycle updates for every Containerlab resource and augments them with interface change notifications collected from the container network namespaces. The output combines the selected runtime's event feed (for example Docker) with the netlink information that powers `containerlab inspect interfaces`, so you can observe container activity and interface state changes in real time without selecting a specific lab.
6: 
7: ## Usage
8: 
9: `containerlab [global-flags] events [local-flags]`
10: 
11: **aliases:** `ev`
12: 
13: The command respects the global flags such as `--runtime`, `--debug`, or `--log-level`. It adds local options:
14: 
15: - `--format` controls the output representation (`plain`, `json`).
16: - `--initial-state` emits a snapshot of currently running containers and their interface states before following live updates.
17: - `--interface-stats` enables periodic interface counter sampling; leave unset to report only lifecycle and state changes.
18: - `--interface-stats-interval` customizes how frequently statistics are collected (for example `500ms`, `2s`, `1m`).
19: 
20: When invoked with no arguments it discovers all running labs and immediately begins streaming events; new labs that start after the command begins are picked up automatically.
21: 
22: ## Event format
23: 
24: In the default `plain` format every line mirrors the `docker events` format:
25: 
26: ```
27: <timestamp> <type> <action> <actor> (<key>=<value>, ...)
28: ```
29: 
30: - **Runtime events** show the short container ID as the actor and include the original attributes supplied by the container runtime (for example `image`, `name`, `containerlab`, `scope`, …). Container events are also enriched with `mgmt_ipv4`, `mgmt_ipv6`, and `ports` (published/exposed ports) when those values are available. When `--initial-state` is enabled the stream starts with `container <state>` snapshots (for example `container running`) that carry an `origin=snapshot` attribute.
31: - **Interface events** use type `interface` and `origin=netlink` in the attribute list. They also report interface-specific data such as `ifname`, `state`, `mtu`, `mac`, `type`, `alias`, and the lab label. The actor is still the container short ID, and the container name is supplied in the attributes (`name=...`).
32: - Interface notifications are emitted when a link appears, disappears, or when its relevant properties (operational state, MTU, alias, MAC address, type) change. Initial snapshots use the `snapshot` action when `--initial-state` is requested. When interface statistics are enabled the stream also includes `interface stats` updates with byte/packet counters and rate estimates.
33: 
34: When `--format json` is used, each event becomes a single JSON object on its own line. The fields match the plain output (`timestamp`, `type`, `action`, `actor_id`, `actor_name`, `actor_full_id`) and include an `attributes` map with the same key/value pairs that the plain formatter prints.
35: 
36: ## Examples
37: 
38: ### Watch an existing lab and new deployments
39: 
40: ```
41: $ containerlab events
42: 2024-07-01T11:02:56.123456000Z container start 5d0b5a9ad3f1 (containerlab=frr-lab, image=ghcr.io/srl-labs/frr, name=clab-frr-lab-frr01, ports=0.0.0.0:2222/tcp->22;0.0.0.0:830/tcp->830)
43: 2024-07-01T11:02:57.004321000Z interface create 5d0b5a9ad3f1 (ifname=eth0, index=22, lab=frr-lab, mac=02:42:ac:14:00:02, mtu=1500, name=clab-frr-lab-frr01, origin=netlink, state=up, type=veth)
44: 2024-07-01T11:02:57.104512000Z interface update 5d0b5a9ad3f1 (ifname=eth0, index=22, lab=frr-lab, mac=02:42:ac:14:00:02, mtu=9000, name=clab-frr-lab-frr01, origin=netlink, state=up, type=veth)
45: 2024-07-01T11:05:12.918273000Z container die 5d0b5a9ad3f1 (containerlab=frr-lab, exitCode=0, image=ghcr.io/srl-labs/frr, name=clab-frr-lab-frr01)
46: 2024-07-01T11:05:13.018456000Z interface delete 5d0b5a9ad3f1 (ifname=eth0, index=22, lab=frr-lab, name=clab-frr-lab-frr01, origin=netlink, state=up, type=veth)
47: ```
48: 
49: The stream contains all currently running labs and stays active to capture subsequent deployments, restarts, or interface adjustments.
50: 
51: ### Include existing resources in the stream
52: 
53: ```
54: $ containerlab events --initial-state
55: 2024-07-01T11:02:55.912345000Z container running 5d0b5a9ad3f1 (containerlab=frr-lab, image=ghcr.io/srl-labs/frr, name=clab-frr-lab-frr01, origin=snapshot, ports=0.0.0.0:2222/tcp->22;0.0.0.0:830/tcp->830, state=running)
56: 2024-07-01T11:02:55.912678000Z interface snapshot 5d0b5a9ad3f1 (ifname=eth0, index=22, lab=frr-lab, mac=02:42:ac:14:00:02, mtu=1500, name=clab-frr-lab-frr01, origin=netlink, state=up, type=veth)
57: …
58: ```
59: 
60: This mode begins with a point-in-time view of every running container and interface before switching to live updates.
61: 
62: ### Include interface statistics
63: 
64: ```
65: containerlab events --interface-stats
66: ```
67: 
68: Statistics are disabled by default. Enabling them augments the feed with periodic counter samples in addition to lifecycle and state changes. Use `--interface-stats-interval` to balance fidelity with overhead: values between `1s` and `5s` work well for most labs, while larger deployments may prefer longer intervals (for example `10s`) to avoid excessive sampling load.
69: 
70: ### Use with alternative runtimes
71: 
72: Containerlab streams events from the runtime selected via the global `--runtime` flag.
73: 
74: Currently supported runtimes:
75: 
76: - `docker`
77: - `c9s`
78: 
79: With `--runtime c9s`, events are backed by kubernetes watches for Clabernetes
80: `Topology` resources and labeled Pods. Interface statistics are sampled inside
81: the device containers, not through local host netlink.
82: 
83: Runtimes that do not implement the `events` API, or are not yet supported by Containerlab, will exit with an explanatory error.
84: 
85: ## See also
86: 
87: - [`inspect interfaces`](inspect/interfaces.md) – produces a point-in-time view of the same interface details that `events` reports continuously.
88: - [Clabernetes containerlab runtime](../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md) - explains how c9s events differ from Docker events.
89: - `docker events` – the raw runtime feed that Containerlab builds upon.

(End of file - total 89 lines)

And the library behavior with ErrorCallback: from `subscribe.go` in vishvananda/netlink (added in PR #787 "Add error callback for netlink subscriptions" or similar), the pattern in all `*Subscribe*` functions:

```go
msgs, from, err := s.Receive()
if err != nil {
    if done != nil {
        select {
        case <-done:
            return
        default:
        }
    }
    if s.GetReceiveErrorFunc() != nil {
        // Pending error handler is set, so call it and do not return
        s.HandleReceiveError(err)
        continue
    }
    // error is not misbehavior, perhaps the socket was closed
    return
}
```

I'm fairly confident of this. The consequences as analyzed. I'll present it as a P2 with the caveat that the vendored source isn't in the snapshot and recommend verifying against the module source.

Hmm, wait — actually one more consideration on the direction of the fix. If the author's intent was: "errors during the initial listing are expected (listener races), don't kill the subscription for them" — then the callback approach makes sense, but then the resubscribe machinery (the `!ok` branch) is unnecessary and the reconciliation should be driven differently. But the PR clearly built the resubscribe path (`run` loop, `processExisting` with `initial=false`, `removeVanishedLinks`, tests `TestProcessExistingAfterResubscribe`) and the comment says "until ctx ends or the subscription fails". The `!ok` branch is meant to catch subscription failure — but with ErrorCallback set it never fires. So either:
(a) drop ErrorCallback → receive errors close the channel → `!ok` fires → resubscribe with reconciliation (states persisted). This makes the whole design work as intended. The only behavior change: transient Receive errors (ENOBUFS) now cause a resubscribe + reconciliation instead of silent message loss — strictly better.
(b) keep the callback → remove the dead resubscribe code.

Recommend (a).

One caveat on (a): with the callback removed, an error during the initial listing closes the channel mid-dump → resubscribe → re-lists → correct recovery. Good.

Also, about `lastError`: with (a), `lastError`/`errMu` are unnecessary — the `!ok` branch can use a generic error. Simpler.

Now severity assessment. Is P2 right? The PR's core purpose is resilience to subscription loss; the mechanism that delivers it never runs. Users get silently dropped notifications (e.g., ENOBUFS under load) with no reconciliation — a correctness/reliability defect relative to the PR's intent, though not a regression vs base (base just died silently... actually base died entirely, losing ALL future events; head keeps receiving future events but loses dropped ones). So head is better than base, but the advertised mechanism doesn't work. P2 (correctness/reliability defect) fits.

Also let me double check the exact claim about the library once more, because the whole P2 hinges on it. Key evidence available in the snapshot: the PR author's own comment: "An interrupted listing is reported here too. It needs no action: links that changed during the listing also arrive as updates." — This tells us the author KNOWS the ErrorCallback fires during interrupted listings and deliberately chose not to resubscribe for that case. So the author's design intent: ErrorCallback absorbs transient errors; resubscribe triggers only when the channel closes. But under the library's actual semantics, the channel never closes while a callback is registered — so the author's intent cannot be realized. This is consistent with my analysis. Note also: if the author had tested the resubscribe path in production (e.g., by killing the socket), they'd have noticed. The unit tests only test processExisting/processUpdate directly, and the integration tests don't exercise resubscribe (they can't easily). So the dead path went unnoticed. Solid P2.

One more scenario where channel closes WITH callback: the library goroutine exits if `done` is closed (only after watch returns) or... if `LinkSubscribeWithOptions`'s goroutine panics. Not realistic. Also, socket read error that is not recoverable — with callback, loop continues forever (each error → callback → continue). If the fd is somehow closed externally (e.g., fd exhaustion?) — the goroutine would spin hot: Receive → EBADF → callback → continue → Receive → ... a busy loop with Debug logging (suppressed at normal levels). Hot spin risk exists in the current design. With the callback removed, the goroutine returns and closes the channel → resubscribe. Another argument for fix (a).

# Code Review: netlink watcher resilience (resubscribe + gap reconciliation)

## Summary

The PR substantially reworks `core/events/netlink.go` so that the per-container netlink watcher can retry a failed subscription, survive subscription termination, and reconcile links that changed while no subscription was active. The overall design is sound and the changes are surgical: a retry loop with capped exponential backoff in `run`, `ListExisting: true` on the subscription, listing replies distinguished from notifications via the `NLM_F_MULTI` flag, persisted `states`/`statsSamples` maps across subscriptions, and `removeVanishedLinks` for missed deletions. The new test file covers listing-vs-notification races, retry behavior, and give-up after repeated failures, with careful netns lifecycle handling.

The central problem is that the mechanism the PR is built around — resubscribing after the subscription ends — is effectively unreachable. The subscription is configured with an `ErrorCallback`, and in `github.com/vishvananda/netlink` (v1.3.1 in `go.mod`) a registered receive-error handler makes the library's subscription goroutine call the callback and `continue` the receive loop instead of returning and closing the updates channel. As a result, `updates` only ever closes after `done` closes — which happens exactly when `watch` is already returning — so the `case !ok` resubscribe branch, the reconciliation logic behind it, and the captured `lastError` are dead code in production.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[watch: subscribe with ErrorCallback] --> B[library receive goroutine]
    B -->|Receive error| C{ErrorCallback set?}
    C -->|yes| D[call callback, continue loop]
    C -->|no| E[goroutine returns, closes updates]
    D -->|channel never closes| F["watcher: case !ok unreachable<br/>no resubscribe, no gap reconciliation"]
    E -->|only after done closed| G[watcher already returned]
```

## Findings

| Priority | Title |
| --- | --- |
| P2 | Resubscribe/gap-recovery path is unreachable because `ErrorCallback` keeps the netlink subscription alive |
| P4 | `removeVanishedLinks` can race with queued listing replies after a resubscribe, emitting a false `create` |

### P2: Resubscribe/gap-recovery path is unreachable because `ErrorCallback` keeps the netlink subscription alive

**Location:** [`core/events/netlink.go#L372-L435`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/2e29fac504a97d551c4efcc4ca87683b16f263a4/core/events/netlink.go#L372-L435) (head)

**Problem:** `watch` sets `ErrorCallback` on `netlink.LinkSubscribeOptions` and then treats a closed `updates` channel (the `case !ok` branch at line 424) as the signal that the subscription ended, returning `(true, err)` so `run` resubscribes, resets `initial`, and reconciles missed changes via `removeVanishedLinks` and `processExisting` with `initial=false`. However, in `github.com/vishvananda/netlink` v1.3.1, when a receive-error handler is registered, the library's subscription goroutine calls the handler and **continues** its receive loop on `Receive` errors (the library's own comment is "Pending error handler is set, so call it and do not return"); the goroutine returns and closes the channel only when no handler is set. With the callback registered, the channel therefore closes only via `defer close(done)` — which runs when `watch` itself is already returning on `ctx.Done()`. The `!ok` branch is consequently unreachable: the resubscribe loop in `run` never fires after a successful subscription, `lastError`/`errMu` are never read, and the entire gap-recovery design (`processExisting` with `initial=false`, `removeVanishedLinks` on resubscribe) is dead in production. The PR's own comment ("An interrupted listing is reported here too. It needs no action") shows the author relies on the callback for listing interruptions, but the same callback also absorbs errors during steady-state operation where recovery *is* needed.

**Trigger:** A netlink receive error on the subscription socket in steady state — for example `ENOBUFS` when the socket buffer overflows under a burst of link events in a large lab, or any persistent receive error. The subscription keeps delivering subsequent messages (so this is an improvement over base, which silently died on the first error), but messages dropped by the error are never recovered: the deleted link stays in `states` forever (no `delete` event is ever emitted for it), and missed attribute changes surface only if a later notification for the same link happens to differ from the stale state.

**Impact:** The PR's headline feature — automatic resubscription and gap reconciliation — never engages, so `events` output can silently diverge from reality after dropped notifications. Two integration tests exercise the first subscription only; nothing can exercise resubscription because it cannot happen.

**Correction:** Per the simplest-working-solution rule, drop `ErrorCallback` (and with it `lastError`/`errMu`) so that a `Receive` error makes the library goroutine return and close `updates`; the already-implemented `!ok` → resubscribe → re-list → reconcile flow then works exactly as designed, and interrupted listings self-heal via the re-listing on the next attempt. Confirm against the vendored/module source of v1.3.1 before merging (see coverage note), and consider a one-line note in `docs/cmd/events.md` that after a resubscribe, pre-existing interfaces are re-reported as `create` events.

### P4: `removeVanishedLinks` can race with queued listing replies after a resubscribe, emitting a false `create`

**Location:** [`core/events/netlink.go#L394-L396`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/2e29fac504a97d551c4efcc4ca87683b16f263a4/core/events/netlink.go#L394-L396) (head)

**Problem:** After a successful resubscribe, the library has already queued (or is still generating) `NLM_F_MULTI` listing replies for a dump taken at subscribe time, while `removeVanishedLinks` separately calls `LinkList` to detect links deleted during the subscription-less gap. If a tracked link is deleted between the dump generation and the `LinkList` (its `RTM_DELLINK` was lost in the gap), `removeVanishedLinks` correctly emits `delete` and removes it from `states`, but the stale listing reply then arrives and `processExisting` emits a false `create` for the now-nonexistent link and re-adds it to `states`, where it lingers. Conversely, if the link is deleted after the `LinkList` but before the dump is processed, no `delete` is ever emitted. Both variants stem from reconciling with two independently taken snapshots.

**Trigger:** Only reachable once the P2 fix activates the resubscribe path; a link deletion landing in the milliseconds-wide window between the subscription's dump snapshot and the `removeVanishedLinks` listing.

**Impact:** One spurious `create` event per race occurrence plus a stale `states` entry that persists until the interface index is reused; cosmetic event-stream inaccuracy, no resource growth.

**Correction:** Drive reconciliation from a single source of truth: either run `removeVanishedLinks` only after the listing replies have been consumed, or derive deletes from the listing itself. Given the tiny window, an optional improvement.

## Coverage notes

- Both changed paths were reviewed in full: `head/core/events/netlink.go` (all 1216 lines, including `run`, `watch`, `processExisting`, `removeVanishedLinks`, `processUpdate`, `pollNetemChanges`, `collectAndEmitStats`, and the netem querier), the new `netlink_watch_test.go` (all 375 lines), the base `netlink.go` regions shown in `diff.txt`, plus `core/events/stream.go`, `core/events/types.go`, `core/events/netlink_test.go` (no helper-name collisions with the new test file; no package-var conflicts), `go.mod`, and `docs/cmd/events.md`.
- **Verification caveat:** `github.com/vishvananda/netlink` v1.3.1 is not vendored in the snapshot, so the P2 analysis of `ErrorCallback` semantics is based on the library's subscribe implementation as known for this version, not on in-repo source. The finding is corroborated by the PR's own comment acknowledging that the callback absorbs listing errors; please verify against the module source before merging.
- **Tests not executed:** this is a source-only review; the new integration tests require root and real network namespaces and were inspected, not run. Their netns lifecycle handling (`LockOSThread`, cleanup ordering, non-`Fatal` `t.Errorf` in the `wg.Go` goroutine) is correct.
- Tests mutate package-level `watchRetryDelay`/`watchMaxAttempts` with `t.Cleanup` restore; this is safe today because no test in the package uses `t.Parallel()`, but would race if parallelization is added later.
- If the P2 fix activates resubscription, note the semantic wrinkle that a first subscription whose initial listing fails reports pre-existing interfaces as `create` rather than `snapshot` on the retry, deviating mildly from `docs/cmd/events.md`'s "Initial snapshots use the `snapshot` action" wording; a doc note is proportionate.
- No topology/configuration API changes are involved, so no schema comparison was needed.
